question: Which mixed-layer-depth criterion should be the headline: sigma-theta increase of 0.03 or 0.125 kg m-3 from a 10 m reference, and is 10 m the reference depth?
context: Rasmus (2026-09-16): 'when density has increased by this much, I forgot exactly how much, but I can look it up'. All three are published (mld_sigma_theta_003, mld_sigma_theta_0125, mld_temperature_02); on 2025-04-3322 the medians were 20, 32 and 25 m. CalCOFI/workflows#101.
proposed_answer: ADOPTED 2026-10-01 (Ben Best approved the provider position): headline MLD = depth where sigma-theta exceeds the 10 m reference by 0.02 kg m-3 (the CalCOFI legacy definition); our earlier proposal (0.03, de Boyer Montegut et al. 2004) is superseded as the headline.

Also (inline comment in "Next Two Weeks Tasks"): "I suggest we use the CalCOFI legacy definition established by Ralf. +0.02 kg/m3 below 10 m. label: Q02
question: Chlorophyll-a maximum and integral: is a 5 m running median right before taking the maximum, and is 0-200 m the integration depth (rather than the euphotic depth or the full cast)?
context: Rasmus (2026-09-16): 'whatever depth range where you have a peak in chlorophyll a levels ... integrated chl ... is just summing up all the one meter bin[s]'. est_chlorophyll_a_sta_corr is itself defined over 0-200 m only. CalCOFI/workflows#102.
proposed_answer: ADOPTED 2026-10-01 (Ben Best approved the provider position): DCM = depth of the highest value of a 3 m running mean (replaces our 5 m running median). Integrated chlorophyll: sum the 1 m bins over the top 200 m, or to the cast depth on shallower stations; trapezoid between points for bottle data.
answer: Rasmus Swalethorp (SIO), 2026-09-23, email (inline comments in "Next Two Weeks Tasks", then: "I think I answered these two in my comments above."). Chlorophyll maximum: "We could include this as well. But I would define it as the Depth of Chl a max (DCM). To avoid a potential narrow spike being adopted as the max I suggest we do a 3 m running mean (I was considering 5m but sometimes the layers can be pretty narrow), and call the depth of the highest value within that running mean the DCM." Integrated chlorophyll: "For the CTD data here we should just sum up all the 1m bins within the top 200m or as deep as the station was on shallower stations. For the bottle data we will need to integrate between points. I believe trapezoidal integration was used in the past".
